questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to organise a children's birthday party
Birthday cakes, from simple ones to works of art
Why people celebrate birthdays in different countries
The health problems of eating too much cake
questions.why: They hear from two bakers: one who makes simple cakes and one who makes personalised creations.

questions.q: Why does Beth sing “Happy Birthday” at the start?
options: Because it is Neil's birthday that day
Because she wants to practise for a party
To introduce the topic of the programme
Because it is her own birthday
questions.why: She knows it's not his birthday, but “this programme is all about birthdays”.

questions.q: How have birthday cakes changed, according to Beth?
options: They have become much smaller
People have stopped putting candles on them because of safety
They are now usually made with less sugar
Many are now designed and decorated to represent the person
questions.why: She says many are now works of art designed to represent the person celebrating.

questions.q: What flavours does Dame Mary Berry want in her perfect cake?
options: Lemon or orange
Chocolate or coffee
Strawberry or vanilla
Banana or carrot
questions.why: She says lemon or orange are her favourite flavours.

questions.q: What matters most to Mary Berry in a birthday cake?
options: Fresh, good flavour rather than perfect decoration
A design that shows the person's hobbies and interests
Many layers and bright colours
Being bought from a famous shop
questions.why: She doesn't mind if it's “higgledy-piggledy” as long as it's fresh and well flavoured.

questions.q: Why do Adam Cox's customers leave the design to him?
options: They don't have enough time to think about it themselves
He refuses to follow instructions
His cakes are cheaper that way
They've seen his earlier designs and trust him
questions.why: He says clients give him leeway based on the past designs of his that they've seen.

questions.q: How does Adam come up with decoration ideas?
options: He copies cakes from TV programmes
He learns about the person's interests and hobbies
He asks Mary Berry for advice
He uses exactly the same design for every single customer
questions.why: Neil says Adam finds out about the person's interests and hobbies and uses them.

questions.q: How does Adam feel about his job?
options: Tired, because clients ask for too much
Worried, because cakes don't last long
Happy, because it lets him be creative
Bored, because the work is repetitive
questions.why: He says it's a real pleasure because it gives him freedom to express himself creatively.
